students.heroTitle: Free Tools for Every Filipino Student
students.heroSubtitle: Everything you need for school — writing, presentations, photos, video, coding, and study — without paying for a single app.
students.goalsTitle: What do you want to do?
students.goalsSubtitle: Pick a task and we’ll show free tools that do the job.
students.pathsSubtitle: Step-by-step toolkits that take you from zero to confident.
students.altSubtitle: Swap expensive apps for free ones that do the same job.

tip1.title: Keep notes in one place
tip1.text: Pick one notes app (like Joplin or Obsidian) and put everything there, so you can always find it later.

tip2.title: Back up your work
tip2.text: Save important files to a free cloud like Nextcloud, or keep a copy on a USB drive, so you never lose a deadline.

tip3.title: Learn a few shortcuts
tip3.text: A handful of keyboard shortcuts — copy, paste, undo, save — will save you hours over a school year.

tip4.title: Work offline when data is low
tip4.text: Most tools here run without internet. Download once and keep working even when you’re out of data.

faq.q1: Do I have to pay for anything?
faq.a1: No. Every tool here is free and open-source. There are no trials that expire and no hidden fees.
faq.q2: Do I need to make an account?
faq.a2: No account is needed to use Abakada, and most tools work without signing up. Some optional cloud features may offer a free account.
faq.q3: Will these work on my phone?
faq.a3: Many do, and some are phone-first. Each tool page lists the platforms it supports — look for Android or iOS.
faq.q4: Can I use these for schoolwork?
faq.a4: Yes. These tools create standard files — documents, images, video — you can submit anywhere, perfect for reports, projects, and presentations.

educators.guideTitle: How to introduce open source to your students

step1.title: Start with one tool
step1.text: Pick a single tool that maps to your next lesson — LibreOffice Writer for worksheets, or GIMP for image editing — instead of changing everything at once.

step2.title: Model it first
step2.text: Demonstrate the tool yourself on a projector or shared screen so students see the workflow before they try it.

step3.title: Give a small, real task
step3.text: Have students produce something they would have made anyway — a report, a poster, an audio clip — using the free tool.

step4.title: Point to the official help
step4.text: Each tool page links to the official site and documentation. Encourage students to learn to find answers themselves.

educators.parentSubtitle: Quick answers to the questions families ask most.

parent.q1: Is this software safe for my child?
parent.a1: Yes. Every tool is open-source and reviewed before listing, and we link only to official download sites. Open-source code can be publicly inspected, which is one reason schools and governments worldwide trust it.
parent.q2: Does my child need to create an account?
parent.a2: No. Abakada requires no sign-up, and the tools we highlight for classrooms can be used without creating accounts. Some optional online services may offer a free account to save work.
parent.q3: Will these run on our home computer?
parent.a3: Almost certainly. We prioritise tools that run on Windows, macOS, and Linux, including older and lower-spec machines, and many work offline.
parent.a4: Abakada is an independent, volunteer-driven project. We align our learning paths to DepEd Senior High School strands for relevance, but we are not an official DepEd program.

about.title: About Us
about.pageTitle: About Us - Abakada | Free Tools for Filipino Students & Educators
about.heroSubtitle: Empowering every Filipino with free, accessible productivity tools—from students in remote barangays to educators shaping the next generation.
about.missionText1: Abakada is dedicated to serving all people of the Philippines by providing free access to powerful productivity tools. We believe that quality software should never be a barrier to education or success.
about.missionText2: Our special focus is on supporting underprivileged scholars who deserve the same digital resources as their peers. By curating the best free and open-source tools, we help level the playing field for every Filipino learner.
about.educatorsText1: We provide specialized glossary tools designed to assist teachers in educational instruction. These resources help educators explain complex concepts, create learning materials, and enhance classroom engagement.
about.educatorsText2: From lesson planning to student assessment, our curated collection supports teachers across all subjects and grade levels throughout the Philippines.
about.visionText1: We envision a Philippines where every student—regardless of economic background or geographic location—has access to the same powerful digital tools as their peers worldwide.
about.visionText2: By curating and promoting free, open-source alternatives to expensive software, we're helping bridge the digital divide one tool at a time.
about.valuesSubtitle: The principles that guide everything we do at Abakada.
about.valueAccessibilityText: Free tools for everyone, everywhere in the Philippines.
about.valueQualityText: Only the best open-source tools make it to our collection.
about.valueCommunityText: Built by Filipinos, for Filipinos, with love.
about.valueOpenSourceText: Transparency and collaboration at our core.
about.storyText1: Abakada was born from a simple observation: many Filipino students struggle to access the same digital tools that their peers in wealthier countries take for granted. Expensive software licenses create barriers that shouldn't exist in education.
about.storyText2: We started by compiling a list of free alternatives to popular paid software. What began as a personal resource quickly grew into something bigger—a comprehensive directory designed specifically for the Filipino context, with tools that work offline, on older hardware, and in areas with limited internet connectivity.
about.storyText3: Today, Abakada serves students, educators, and professionals across the Philippines, helping them discover powerful tools that cost nothing but deliver everything.
